title: The Battle of Šalba (Xelva). With the Catalans broken, the Emperor must give battle on bad ground, hills, forest and a river, against nearly twice his numbers. His horse tries to sweep away both Castilian flanks before their numbers tell, and the centre holds by a thread; but the wings are worn down and the field is lost. A month of fighting costs al-Andalus and its ṭāʾifas 8,170 men against Castile's 7,520, and 12 points of war score

data.terrain: the defender had +5 from the ground; dice ran 8–7 and 4–5

source: Trent's account and battle screens, 13 December 1375 to 14 January 1376

title: After Šalba another 2,000 men are levied from the nobles

Envoys ride for Fās. Since the last war there has been a warm silence between the courts: not hostile, but distrustful on ours, for the Marīnids courted the Emirate and then stabbed it in the back the moment they could. Now Duʿā argues for renewing the alliance; the expanded bureaucracy can bear it, and the first Mamlūk army is months away. The crown prince of Fās, Abū al-Faḍl, has lately married the Emperor's sister Jadīla, and that and Duʿā open the dialogue. A pact is offered. Morocco's truce with Castile runs to September 1377, but if its words are to be believed, and that is questionable, it is willing to help

title: Defeat in detail. The Pope lands an army on the Catalan coast, a foolish venture, and the Emperor falls on it before Girona: 8,400 against 2,900. In a day 2,250 of the Pope's men are lost for 234 of ours
source: Trent's account and battle screens, 24–25 May 1376

title: Siena follows its master's footsteps. Before Girona again, the Sienese come against the Emperor's 8,200 with 1,560 and are destroyed to the last man, for 101 of ours
source: Trent's account and battle screen, 12 June 1376

title: A Castilian army has Barcelona under siege. The Emperor turns to a well-tried strategy, the mercenaries and the faithful of the wars of 1339 and after, and raises more than 7,000 veterans from the Marches to break the siege

data.raised: 7,000+ veterans from the Marches (mercenaries and volunteers of the faith)
data.purpose: to relieve Barcelona, under siege by a Castilian army
data.precedent: the mercenaries and mutaṭawwiʿa of the 1339 host
data.date: June 1376, after the second battle of Girona (Trent); the exact size awaits a save or screen

title: The Moors cannot join the war while their truce with Castile holds, but they send a gift of gold into the Emperor's treasury, freely given. The mercenaries are expensive, and the gift keeps them in the field

data.note: the gift's exact size is not on the screens; the treasury rose by about 850 in two months while paying the mercenaries

source: Trent's account and screenshots of 12 June and 16 August 1376

title: The second great battle of the war is joined at Agramunt, in the Catalan plain below the Pyrenees: the Emperor's 13,400, with the mercenaries of the Marches, Valencia and the Algarve, against 18,350 Castilians under the general who won at Šalba
